analysis.title: Fiserv Inc. (FISV): 3Q26 Key Takeaways: Reiterated outlook and improved retention trends demonstrates progress on the multi-year turnaround
key_insights: Shares outperformed after the print. GS believes investors feared another guidance revision against a steep ramp in implied 4Q guidance, so reiterated FY2026 guidance was well received.
Core conversion declined 25% YTD after doubling, which GS reads as roughly half of the increased churn having abated.
The company expects to exit 2026 around its medium-term targets in both segments, adjusting for divestitures.
Capital return is picking up: $500mn planned in 4Q with a further step up indicated for 2027, while cash flow conversion remains 90%+.

GS expects the pace of improvement to moderate because attrition in the banking segment takes a long time to flow through the income statement (lengthy deconversion timelines) and new client wins take time to implement.
GS stays Neutral and on the sidelines, expecting the turnaround to take time to fully take effect, though it sees the quarter as pointing in the right direction.
3Q26 adjusted revenue was ~$4.85bn, in line with Visible Alpha consensus, -1% y/y. Merchant Solutions was -3% (-2% organic) and Financial Solutions was flat (-4% organic).
3Q26 adjusted operating income was ~$1.51bn, in line with the Street, at a 31.2% margin. Adjusted EPS was $1.75 vs the Street's $1.71.
Merchant Solutions missed on profit: operating income was $724mn vs Street $795mn, with a 28.7% margin vs 30.8% expected. Revenue was ~$2.52bn vs VA consensus ~$2.58bn.
Clover GPV rose 9% reported (11% excluding gateway conversion), Clover processing revenue rose 12%, and Clover revenue growth was 1% reported.
Financial Solutions beat: adjusted revenue ~$2.33bn vs VA consensus ~$2.28bn, operating income $887mn, margin 38.1% vs Street 37.4%.

FY2026 guidance reaffirmed: organic growth -1% to 0%, adjusted revenue growth -1.5% to -0.5%, adjusted operating margin 31%-31.5%, adjusted EPS $7.20-$7.40 (about -17% to -14% y/y), FCF conversion ~90% (about $3.5bn FCF).
GS raised its 12-month price target to $61 from $56, on an unchanged ~7x multiple on Q5-Q8 EPS. GS 2026/2027/2028 EPS estimates are now $7.29/$8.13/$9.34 (previously $7.26/$7.81/$8.62).

market_movers.rationale: PT raised to $61 from $56 on an unchanged ~7x multiple on Q5-Q8 EPS. Neutral kept because the turnaround will take time to fully take effect.
